original_question: Does every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) have vertex-connectivity at least (2 delta(G) + 1) / 3?
target_in_paper: Section 2.6, Conjecture 6: the point-visibility-graph connectivity conjecture asking whether every visibility graph with minimum degree δ has vertex-connectivity at least (2δ+1)/3.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost verbatim: it asks about every visibility graph, uses the correct parameter δ(G) (minimum degree), the correct conclusion about vertex-connectivity, and the correct lower bound (2δ(G)+1)/3. It is very close to the paper's official formulation.
missing_details: The paper's conjecture is in the point-visibility section, so 'visibility graph' should be specified as the visibility graph of a finite set of points in the plane, not a segment-visibility graph or polygon-visibility graph.
The question should define adjacency: two vertices are adjacent exactly when the corresponding points are mutually visible, i.e. the segment joining them contains no other point of the set.
The notation κ(G) for vertex-connectivity and δ(G) for minimum degree should be stated explicitly to make the question stand-alone.
It should be clear that no general-position assumption is imposed: collinearities are allowed; the conjecture is meant for all point visibility graphs.

Since κ(G) is integer-valued while (2δ(G)+1)/3 may be nonintegral, the paper states the bound exactly in that rational form, without adding a ceiling; that implicit convention can be left as is but should be understood.
refined_question: Let G be the visibility graph of a finite set P of points in the plane, with no restriction on collinearities, where two vertices are adjacent if and only if the segment joining the corresponding points contains no other point of P. Must the vertex-connectivity κ(G) satisfy κ(G) ≥ (2δ(G)+1)/3, where δ(G) is the minimum degree of G?
justification: This draft is aiming at the survey's official Conjecture 6 in Section 2.6, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 1 gives the point-visibility definition, and Section 2.6 introduces the graph-theoretic notation κ(G), λ(G), and δ(G) before stating Theorems 5 and 6 as partial lower bounds and then Conjecture 6 as the sharper general bound. The only substantive omissions in the draft are the planar point-set interpretation of 'visibility graph,' the definition of visibility, and the notation for connectivity.
